#Build a similarity network and cut into clusters
Build a similarity network, 
  first for all the samples for exploration
  then with the '700 sample' removed as it simply acts too much like an outlier
  then with just the EDS samples, as that is what we want to cluster
  then with the clusters visualized
```{r similarity_network}
#Get some group information that can be used for color labels
healthy_group <- rownames(metadata)[grep("healthy", metadata[,"disease_state"])]
EDS_group <- rownames(metadata)[grep("EDS-HT", metadata[,"disease_state"])]
Male_group <- rownames(metadata)[grep("Male", metadata[,"inferred_sex"])]
Female_group <- rownames(metadata)[grep("Female", metadata[,"inferred_sex"])]

if (RUN_PLOTS){
  #Using all the data
  Fun_heatmap(data_matrix = t(data),
              title = "Heatmap of all the data",
              col_side = "sex",
              xlab = "Sex",
              row_side = "disease",
              ylab = "Disease")
}
if (RUN_PLOTS){
  #Without GSM8336700
    #700 keeps acting like an outlier, wanted to see how the similarity would look without it
  Fun_heatmap(data_matrix = t(data[,colnames(data) != "GSM8336700"]),
              title = "Heatmap without GSM8336700",
              col_side = "sex",
              xlab = "Sex",
              row_side = "disease",
              ylab = "Disease")
}
if (RUN_PLOTS){
  #With only the EDS samples
  Fun_heatmap(data_matrix = t(data[,EDS_group]),
              title = "Heatmap - Only EDS",
              col_side = "sex",
              xlab = "Sex",
              row_side = "disease",
              ylab = "Disease")
}
if (RUN_PLOTS){
  #With 2 clusters
  Fun_heatmap(data_matrix = t(data[,EDS_group]),
              clusters = 2,
              title = "Heatmap - Clustered EDS",
              col_side = "cluster",
              xlab = "Cluster",
              row_side = "sex",
              ylab = "Sex")
}

```

```{r clusters}
#Use the same code inside the function to get the clusters out and into the metadata
#Compute similarity using correlation
#Correlation as I want to compare patterns
sim_obj <- simil(t(data[,EDS_group]), 
                  method = "correlation",
                  pairwise = TRUE) 
#Convert to a matrix 
sim_matrix <- as.matrix(sim_obj)
#Set the self-correlation to 1 as the function gives a self correlation of zero back
diag(sim_matrix) <- 1

#Get out some clusters by creating a dist_matrix as well
dist_matrix <- 1-sim_matrix
diag(dist_matrix) <- 0
dist_matrix <- as.dist(dist_matrix)
  
#Get dendrogram
hc <- hclust(dist_matrix, method = "complete")

#Cut into 2 clusters
clusters_k <- cutree(hc, 2)
clusters_k <- as.data.frame(clusters_k)
#Set the controls to cluster 0 so that the information can be added to the broader metadata file
clusters_k[healthy_group,] <- 0

#Add the cluster information to the metadata
metadata <- merge(metadata, clusters_k, by = "row.names")
rownames(metadata) <- metadata$Row.names
metadata$Row.names <- NULL
```


#wilcox.test
Performing a wilcox test to find p_values between the clusters 
  Note to myself: I tested if the results of the p-values would change if I unlogged the data, the p-values seem to stay the same as this source also mentions (https://stats.stackexchange.com/questions/178744/how-do-logarithmic-measurements-affect-the-wilcoxon-rank-sum-test)
```{r wilcox_test}
#TAG: If time allows, make the code more modular so it can handle more than 2 clusters
#Get cluster identifiers inside a list
  #The length of the list is dependent on the amount of unique values in metadata[,"clusters_k"] minus 1 (to account for the cluster 0 controls)
cluster_list <- list()
for (cluster in 1:(length(unique(metadata[,"clusters_k"]))-1)){
cluster_list[[paste0("cluster_",cluster,"_group")]] <- rownames(metadata)[grep(cluster, metadata[,"clusters_k"])]
}

#Set up cluster_1_vs_2 to save the p-value and statistic results
cluster_1_vs_2 <- data.frame(matrix(nrow = nrow(data), ncol = 2))
rownames(cluster_1_vs_2) <- rownames(data)
colnames(cluster_1_vs_2) <- c("p_value","statistic")

for (i in 1:nrow(data)){

#Use the two.sided setting as the goal is not to check if one is greater/less than the other but to see if either one of them are different from the other
res <- wilcox.test((as.double(data[i,unname(unlist(cluster_list[1]))])), 
                   (as.double(data[i,unname(unlist(cluster_list[2]))])), 
                   paired = FALSE, 
                   alternative = "two.sided")
#Save the result
cluster_1_vs_2[i,"p_value"] <- res$p.value
cluster_1_vs_2[i,"statistic"] <- res$statistic
}

#Also add an adjusted p value using FDR
cluster_1_vs_2[,"adj_p_value"] <- p.adjust(cluster_1_vs_2[,"p_value"], method = 'fdr', n = length(cluster_1_vs_2[,"p_value"]))

#Give some feedback
cat(paste0(sum(cluster_1_vs_2[,"p_value"] < 0.05), 
           " (",
           round((sum(cluster_1_vs_2[,"p_value"] < 0.05)/nrow(cluster_1_vs_2))*100,2),
           "%) made it to a p-value of 0.05 or below between the two clusters."))

```
#Get log2FC between the clusters
The formula used to calculate the fold change was found at:
https://www.biostars.org/p/342756/
  --> mean(log2(Group1)) - mean(log2(Group2))
    --> median(log2(Group1)) - median(log2(Group2))
Calculating both as median can handle outliers better on advice from Agi
```{r log2FC}
#As it was assumed that the data was already in log2 notation, the log2FC should be as simple as taking the mean/median and subtracting

#Get the median of the clusters and place it in a df
data.cluster <- data.frame(matrix(nrow = nrow(data),ncol = 0))
rownames(data.cluster) <- rownames(data)

for (i in 1:nrow(data)){
  data.cluster[i,"cluster_1_mean"] <- mean(as.double(data[i,cluster_list$cluster_1_group]))
  data.cluster[i,"cluster_2_mean"] <- mean(as.double(data[i,cluster_list$cluster_2_group]))
  data.cluster[i,"cluster_1_median"] <- median(as.double(data[i,cluster_list$cluster_1_group]))
  data.cluster[i,"cluster_2_median"] <- median(as.double(data[i,cluster_list$cluster_2_group]))
}

#Get the log2FC by subtracting the mean(log2()) / median(log2()) clusters
for (i in 1:nrow(data.cluster)){
  data.cluster[i,"log2FC_mean"] <- data.cluster[i,"cluster_1_mean"] - data.cluster[i,"cluster_2_mean"]
  data.cluster[i,"log2FC_median"] <- data.cluster[i,"cluster_1_median"] - data.cluster[i,"cluster_2_median"]
}

#Print some feedback
head(data.cluster)
```
#Combine the results
Combine the p value and log2FC results into one df
```{r initial_results}
#Set the results, together with the previously found p values to a df
data.results <- merge(data.cluster[,c("log2FC_mean", "log2FC_median")], cluster_1_vs_2[,c("p_value","adj_p_value")], by = "row.names")
rownames(data.results) <- data.results$Row.names
data.results$Row.names <- NULL
```

#Filter for the data to actually use
```{r}
#TAG: Make sure that the descriptions still line up with what is happening
#If the fold change is below 0.58, I disregard that measure as the change is less than 1.5 times
  #This allows me to reduce the amount of data I am dealing with 
  #Using the median because as far as I am aware it is better with dealing with outliers
data.selected <- data.results[abs(data.results[,"log2FC_median"]) > 1,]

#Get quantiles of the adj_p_value
  #I would like to take along at least 25% of the data so that I make sure I don't cut out too much
  #type = 7 is the default, this default is makes use of linear interpolation. I did not change away from the default.
cat("What the adjusted pvalues are at these probabilities:\n")
quantile(data.selected[,"adj_p_value"],
         type = 7,
         probs = c(1, 5, 10, 15, 25, 50, 75, 100)/100)
pvalue_cutoff <- quantile(data.selected[,"adj_p_value"],
                           type = 7,
                           probs = 25/100)
cat("\nThe adjusted pvalue at 25%: ",pvalue_cutoff,"\n")

data.selected <- data.selected[data.selected[,"adj_p_value"] <= pvalue_cutoff,]


#print some feedback
cat(nrow(data.selected), "genes made it through the selection.\n")

#Convert to something that STRING can work with better
selected_proteins <- gconvert(rownames(data.selected),organism="hsapiens",target="ENTREZGENE",filter_na = F)$target
selected_proteins <- selected_proteins[!is.na(selected_proteins)]

cat(length(selected_proteins),"protein names selected to use in the network.\n")


```

#PCA on only the EDS samples
Display the PCA's that are used to build the background network with and then select the genes that are used to build the STRING background network.
```{r PCA_on_disease}
#Subset to only get the patient data
data.disease_only <- data[,EDS_group]

#Run a PCA on the patient only data
PCA.disease_only <- pca(object = t(as.matrix(data.disease_only)), 
                   method = "svd", nPcs = 10, center = TRUE)

cat("The PC's that have 10% or more variance:\n")
PCA.disease_only@R2[PCA.disease_only@R2 > 0.10]
pca_variance_selection <- names(PCA.disease_only@R2[PCA.disease_only@R2 > 0.10])

if (RUN_PLOTS){
  #Visualize the PC's that have 10 or more % variance
  for (PC in 1:length(pca_variance_selection)){
    #PC1 and PC2 are not the clearest variable names to use here, not sure what else could work better though
    PC1 <- pca_variance_selection[PC]
    ifelse(PC != length(pca_variance_selection),
           PC2 <- pca_variance_selection[PC+1],
           PC2 <- pca_variance_selection[1])

    Fun_plot_PCA_scores(PCA = PCA.disease_only, 
                      metadata = metadata, 
                      firstPC = PC1, 
                      secondPC = PC2, 
                      title = paste0("PCA scores (",PC1," vs ",PC2,") of just the patients"))

  }
} else {
  cat("Plot not visualized due to RUN_PLOTS being set to FALSE.\n")
}

#Extract the top genes for the PC's that have 10% or more variance
background_nodes <- NULL
for (PC in 1:length(pca_variance_selection)){
  #TAG: check that the description is still correct
  #Get the 99% value and use it as the threshold
    #Above this value should contain the top 1% of the data that is important for the loadings of this PC
      #This value is chosen somewhat arbitrarily
  threshold <- quantile(abs(PCA.disease_only@loadings[,pca_variance_selection[PC]]),
                         type = 7,
                         probs = 99/100,
                         names = FALSE)

  passed <- abs(PCA.disease_only@loadings[,pca_variance_selection[PC]]) >= threshold
  
  #Save the nodes that are in the top percent
  background_nodes <- c(background_nodes, rownames(PCA.disease_only@loadings[passed,]))
}
#Use unique to remove duplicates
background_nodes <- unique(background_nodes)

cat("Selected", length(background_nodes),"genes to build the background network with.\n")


#Convert to something that STRING can work with better
background_proteins <- gconvert(background_nodes,organism="hsapiens",target="ENTREZGENE",filter_na = F)$target
background_proteins <- background_proteins[!is.na(background_proteins)]

cat(length(background_proteins),"protein names selected to build the background network with.\n")

```

#Build the Cytoscape background network
```{r cytoscape_background_network}
#Build the command to send to Cytoscape
  #use a low cutoff (0.4)
cmd <- paste0(
  'string protein query ',
  'query=', paste(background_proteins, collapse = ", "), ' ',
#  'networkType=full STRING network ',
  'networkType=physical subnetwork ',
  'cutoff=0.4 ',
  'newNetName="Background Network" ',
  'species="Homo sapiens" ',
  'limit=', round(length(background_proteins)*0.5),' ',
  'showFlatNodeDesign=true ',
  'showSTRINGstyleLabels=false ',
  'showStructureImages=false'
  )

#Send the command to Cytoscape to build the network
RCy3::commandsRun(cmd)

#Get the network's SUID
background_networkSuid = getNetworkSuid()


```

```{r}
stop()

#Toss that into Cytoscape just for curiousity
tempSTRING <- rownames(data.selected)

#Check that Cytoscape can be reached

#If this section of code is re-run then the code runs into issues, to prevent this, remove if there is a networkSuid in the environment already and reload it

  cat("networkSuid was already made, removing it and remaking it to prevent issues with the code rerunning.\n")

  rm(networkSuid)
  cat("networkSuid has been deleted and will be remade.\n")

  'string protein query ',
  'query="', tempSTRING, '" ',
  'networkType=full STRING network ',

  'newNetName=Base Network ',
  'species="Homo sapiens" ',

  'showFlatNodeDesign=true ',
  'showSTRINGstyleLabels=false ',
  'showStructureImages=false'
  )

#Send the command to Cytoscape to build the network
RCy3::commandsRun(cmd)

#Get the network's SUID
networkSuid = getNetworkSuid()
```

#Advice from Martina:
(to make it so that I can use this project for MSB1014 as well)
* Remove controls and only compare the patients
* Get the top features from a PCA to build the background network 
* Similarity network of the patients
  * Correlate the patients into 2 or 3 clusters to find patient groups
  
#Advice from Agi:
For two independent groups you should use the Mann–Whitney U test (Wilcoxon rank-sum test) can be applied to each feature. In addition to the p-value, report the fold change (FC) to describe the magnitude and direction of the difference. Since you have outliers use median instead of mean.  Because many features are tested please correct the  p-values for multiple testing using the Benjamini–Hochberg FDR procedure.
